questions.stem: Which of these is NOT part of disaster prevention and recovery?

options.text: Waiting until a disaster happens to decide what to do
options.rationale: Correct choice: planning has to happen beforehand.

options.text: Reducing the likelihood of disruptive events
Restoring operations after an event
Writing and testing recovery plans

questions.explanation: Disaster prevention and recovery means reducing the chance of disruptive events and restoring operations when they happen. Prevention lowers likelihood; recovery restores service.
questions.discriminator_tested: Prevention lowers likelihood; recovery restores service.

questions.stem: Which two are causes of data loss? (Choose two.)

options.text: Ransomware encrypting files
Accidental deletion
Running a tabletop exercise
options.rationale: A discussion exercise doesn't touch data.

options.text: Installing a PDU
options.rationale: Power distribution doesn't cause data loss.

options.text: Labeling a backup tape

questions.explanation: Data loss can come from hardware failure, deletion, corruption, ransomware, or disaster. Backups are the primary defense.
questions.discriminator_tested: Causes of data loss include deletion and ransomware.

questions.stem: Which statement about file-level backups is NOT true?

options.text: On their own, they can rebuild an entire system, operating system included
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: they can't rebuild a whole system alone.

options.text: They are fast and small
They can restore individual files
They back up selected files and folders

questions.explanation: File-level backups cover selected files and folders. They are fast and small and restore individual files, but they can't rebuild a whole system alone.
questions.discriminator_tested: File-level backups can't rebuild a whole system alone.

questions.stem: Which statement about image-based backups is NOT true?

options.text: They are smaller than file-level backups of the same data
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: they are larger, because they capture everything.

options.text: They capture the entire disk or system
They enable a bare-metal restore
They include the OS, applications, settings, and data

questions.explanation: Image-based backups capture the entire disk or system, enabling a full-system (bare-metal) restore. They are larger than file-level backups.
questions.discriminator_tested: Image-based backups enable bare-metal restore and are larger.

questions.stem: Which is NOT a sound basis for prioritizing critical applications in backup and recovery?

options.text: Alphabetical order of the application names
options.rationale: Correct choice: names say nothing about business impact.

options.text: How essential the application is to operations
The revenue impact of losing it
Which other systems depend on it

questions.explanation: Identifying critical applications sets backup frequency and recovery order. The priority comes from business criticality.
questions.discriminator_tested: Priority comes from business criticality.

questions.stem:
For network device backup/restore, an administrator saves router configurations with:

copy running-config tftp:

to a server across the WAN. What is the concern?

options.text: TFTP has no authentication or encryption, so a secure transfer such as SCP or SFTP is preferred
options.rationale: Correct: configs often contain sensitive details.

options.text: The command backs up user data instead of the configuration
The command deletes the router's configuration
options.rationale: It copies the configuration; it doesn't delete it.

options.text: TFTP is too fast to be reliable
options.rationale: Speed isn't the issue; security is.

questions.explanation: Network device backup/restore saves device configurations (for example 'copy running-config' to a remote server). It backs up configs, not user data, and secure transfer is preferred over TFTP.
questions.discriminator_tested: Prefer secure transfer over TFTP.

questions.stem: Among data restoration characteristics, what is the difference between RTO and RPO?

options.text: RTO is how long a restore may take; RPO is how much data loss is tolerable, set by the age of the last backup
RTO is how much data may be lost; RPO is how long the restore may take
They mean the same thing
options.rationale: One is time; the other is data.

options.text: Both measure backup cost

questions.explanation: Data restoration characteristics describe how fast and how current a restore is. RTO is how long (time to restore); RPO is how much data (tolerable loss, set by the age of the last backup).
questions.discriminator_tested: RTO = how long; RPO = how much data.

questions.stem: Which two characteristics of backup media help them survive ransomware and the loss of a site? (Choose two.)

options.text: Being kept offline, disconnected from the network
Being stored offsite
options.rationale: Correct: they survive if the main site is lost.

options.text: Being permanently mounted on the production server
options.rationale: Anything mounted can be encrypted along with the server.

options.text: Being kept in the same room as the servers
options.rationale: A fire or flood takes both.

options.text: Being writable by every user
options.rationale: Broad write access makes them easier to destroy.

questions.explanation: Backup media include disk/NAS, tape, cloud, and removable media, each with trade-offs. Offline or offsite media survive ransomware and site loss.
questions.discriminator_tested: Offline or offsite copies survive ransomware and site loss.

questions.stem: Which two statements about backup methods are correct? (Choose two.)

options.text: An incremental backup copies the changes since the last backup of any type
Restoring from differentials needs the last full backup plus the latest differential
Restoring from incrementals needs only the latest incremental
options.rationale: It needs the full backup plus every incremental since.

options.text: A full backup copies only the files that changed
A differential copies only the changes since the previous differential
options.rationale: A differential copies the changes since the last full backup.

questions.explanation: Backup methods: full (everything), incremental (changes since the last backup of any type), and differential (changes since the last full). Incremental restores need the full plus every incremental; differential restores need the full plus the latest differential.
questions.discriminator_tested: Incremental = since last backup; differential = since last full.

questions.stem: Which statement about backup testing is NOT true?

options.text: A backup that finished without errors is proven to be restorable
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: only a test restore proves it.

options.text: It involves restoring data periodically
It verifies integrity and completeness
It confirms how long a restore takes

questions.explanation: Backup testing means periodically restoring data to verify integrity, completeness, and timing. An untested backup is unproven.
questions.discriminator_tested: An untested backup is unproven.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a common method of online account recovery?

options.text: Physically replacing the laptop's hard drive
options.rationale: Correct choice: that has nothing to do with recovering an online account.

options.text: An email reset link
An SMS code
Recovery codes saved earlier

questions.explanation: Online account recovery resets access through email, phone, recovery codes, or MFA. The recovery channel is itself an attack path, so it must be protected.
questions.discriminator_tested: Online recovery uses email, phone, recovery codes, or MFA.

questions.stem: Which statement about local account recovery is NOT true?

options.text: A central help desk can reset it from the directory
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: local accounts have no central reset.

options.text: Another local administrator can reset it
Recovery media or tools can be used
It may require physical access

questions.explanation: Local account recovery is done by another local administrator or with recovery media and tools. It depends on a second admin account or physical access; there is no central reset.
questions.discriminator_tested: Local accounts have no central reset.

questions.stem: Which statement about domain account recovery is NOT true?

options.text: It requires booting the user's PC from recovery media
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: domain accounts are reset centrally in the directory.

options.text: A domain administrator can reset the account
The help desk can unlock the account
Self-service reset is possible

questions.explanation: Domain account recovery means a domain administrator or the help desk resets or unlocks the account in the directory. It is managed centrally, and self-service reset is possible.
questions.discriminator_tested: Domain recovery is managed centrally.

questions.stem: Which statement about battery backup is NOT true?

options.text: It powers equipment for days during an outage
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: runtime is minutes.

options.text: It provides short-term power
Its runtime is measured in minutes
It bridges until a shutdown or a generator start

questions.explanation: Battery backup provides short-term power during an outage, with runtime in minutes, not hours.
questions.discriminator_tested: Battery runtime is minutes, not hours.

questions.stem: Which statement about a UPS is NOT true?

options.text: It is designed to supply power for days
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: it isn't long-term power.

options.text: It is battery-backed
It conditions the incoming power
It bridges to a graceful shutdown or a generator start

questions.explanation: A UPS is battery-backed power that also conditions the input power. It bridges to a graceful shutdown or a generator start; it is not long-term power.
questions.discriminator_tested: A UPS is not long-term power.

questions.stem: A home office wants the cheapest UPS for a desktop PC and can accept a brief switchover gap. Which UPS fits?

options.text: Standby UPS
options.rationale: Correct: the lowest cost, with a brief switchover gap.

options.text: Online UPS
Line-interactive UPS
options.rationale: Mid-range in cost; more than needed here.

options.text: A diesel generator
options.rationale: Far too much for one PC.

questions.explanation: A standby UPS passes utility power through and switches to battery on failure. It has a brief switchover gap and offers the lowest cost and the least protection.
questions.discriminator_tested: Standby: lowest cost, brief switchover gap.

questions.stem: Which statement about a line-interactive UPS is NOT true?

options.text: It always runs the equipment from the inverter, with zero transfer time
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: that is an online UPS.

options.text: It regulates sags and surges without using the battery
It switches to battery during an outage
It is mid-range in cost

questions.explanation: A line-interactive UPS regulates voltage sags and surges without the battery, then switches on an outage. It handles voltage fluctuation and is mid-range.
questions.discriminator_tested: Line-interactive regulates voltage; online has zero transfer time.

questions.stem: Which statement about an online UPS is NOT true?

options.text: It is the lowest-cost type of UPS
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: it is the highest cost.

options.text: It uses double conversion
It has no transfer time
It gives the best protection

questions.explanation: An online UPS uses double conversion: the equipment always runs from the inverter. It has no transfer time and offers the best protection at the highest cost.
questions.discriminator_tested: Online UPS: best protection, highest cost.

questions.stem: Which two statements about power generators are correct? (Choose two.)

options.text: They provide long-duration backup power
They need fuel and regular testing
They start instantly, with no gap at all
options.rationale: They take time to start, which a UPS bridges.

options.text: They remove the need for a UPS
options.rationale: A UPS is still needed to cover the startup gap.

options.text: They are a type of surge protector
options.rationale: Generators supply power; surge protectors divert spikes.

questions.explanation: Power generators provide long-duration backup power (diesel or natural gas). They take time to start, so a UPS bridges the gap, and they need fuel and testing.
questions.discriminator_tested: Generators provide long-duration power, need fuel and testing, and take time to start.

questions.stem: Which statement about surge protection is NOT true?

options.text: It keeps equipment running during a power outage
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: it covers spikes, not outages.

options.text: It diverts voltage spikes away from equipment
It protects against spikes
It is not a UPS

questions.explanation: Surge protection diverts excess voltage spikes away from equipment. It protects against spikes, not outages, and it is not a UPS.
questions.discriminator_tested: Surge protection covers spikes, not outages.

questions.stem: An administrator needs to power-cycle a hung server's outlet in a rack remotely and to monitor its power draw. Which device fits?

options.text: A switched, metered PDU
options.rationale: Correct: remote outlet control plus monitoring.

options.text: A surge protector
The HVAC system
A standby UPS on its own
options.rationale: A basic UPS doesn't give per-outlet remote control.

questions.explanation: A PDU distributes power to rack equipment; metered and switched versions add monitoring and remote outlet control. It handles distribution, not backup.
questions.discriminator_tested: Metered and switched PDUs add monitoring and remote outlet control.

questions.stem: Which statement about HVAC is NOT true?

options.text: Cooling has nothing to do with business continuity
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: overheating causes failures, so cooling is a continuity control.

options.text: It controls temperature
It controls airflow
It controls humidity

questions.explanation: HVAC controls temperature, airflow, and humidity. Overheating causes failures, so cooling is a continuity control.
questions.discriminator_tested: Cooling is a continuity control.

questions.stem: Which statement about ASHRAE standards for computing environments is NOT true?

options.text: Higher humidity always lowers risk, so rooms should be kept as humid as possible
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: too humid causes condensation and corrosion.

options.text: Air that is too dry raises the risk of static discharge
Air that is too humid causes condensation and corrosion
They recommend roughly 18-27 °C

questions.explanation: ASHRAE standards recommend temperature and humidity ranges for computing environments (about 18-27 °C). Too dry raises static discharge risk; too humid causes condensation and corrosion.
questions.discriminator_tested: Too dry = static; too humid = condensation and corrosion.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a goal of fire suppression?

options.text: Putting as much water as possible into every room, whatever it contains
options.rationale: Correct choice: the system should match the space.

options.text: Extinguishing the fire
Limiting harm to people
Limiting damage to equipment

questions.explanation: Fire suppression extinguishes fires while limiting damage to people and equipment. Match the system to the space: water-based or clean agent.
questions.discriminator_tested: Match the suppression system to the space.

questions.stem: A ladder knocks a sprinkler head in a server room, and water sprays out immediately even though there is no fire. Which kind of system is this, and why?

options.text: A wet pipe system: the pipes are always full, so any opened head releases water at once
A preaction system
options.rationale: Without detection, a preaction system's pipes would still be dry.

options.text: A clean agent system
options.rationale: Clean agents are gases, not water.

options.text: A deluge system
options.rationale: Deluge heads are already open, so there is no head to knock off; they discharge on detection.

questions.explanation: In wet pipe systems, the pipes always hold water, and heat (or damage) opens a head. They are the simplest and fastest, but accidental discharge or leaks can damage electronics.
questions.discriminator_tested: Wet pipe: always full, so accidental discharge is the risk.

questions.stem: Why do dry pipe systems deliver water more slowly than wet pipe systems?

options.text: The pipes hold pressurized gas, which has to escape before water reaches the open head
Their pumps are slower
options.rationale: The gas in the pipes is the cause.

options.text: They use foam
They need two separate detections

questions.explanation: Dry pipe systems keep pressurized gas in the pipes, and water enters after a head opens. They are used where pipes could freeze, with slower water delivery.
questions.discriminator_tested: Dry pipe is slower because the gas has to escape first.

questions.stem: Which statement about preaction systems is NOT true?

options.text: Water stays in the pipes at all times
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: the pipes stay dry until detection.

options.text: The pipes stay dry until detection
A head must then open before water flows out
They are common in data centers

questions.explanation: In preaction systems, the pipes stay dry; water enters only after detection, and a head must then open. The two-step trigger lowers the risk of accidental discharge.
questions.discriminator_tested: Preaction has a two-step trigger.

questions.stem: An aircraft hangar that stores fuel needs to flood an area with water instantly when a fire is detected. Which suppression system fits?

options.text: A deluge system
options.rationale: Correct: massive flow from all open heads for a high-hazard area.

options.text: A preaction system
options.rationale: Built to avoid accidental discharge, not to flood an area instantly.

options.text: A clean agent system
options.rationale: Gas suits enclosed equipment rooms, not a hangar.

options.text: A standard wet pipe system
options.rationale: Its heads open one at a time.

questions.explanation: Deluge systems have open heads that discharge water from all heads on detection. They deliver massive water flow for high-hazard areas.
questions.discriminator_tested: Deluge gives massive flow for high-hazard areas.

questions.stem: Which two statements about clean agent systems are correct? (Choose two.)

options.text: They use a gaseous suppressant
They cause no water damage and leave no residue
They are water-based
They leave a residue that must be cleaned off equipment
They suit only unheated warehouses

questions.explanation: Clean agent systems use gaseous suppression that leaves no residue. With no water damage, they suit equipment rooms.
questions.discriminator_tested: Clean agent: gaseous, no residue, no water damage.

questions.stem: Which statement about halon is NOT true?

options.text: New halon production is encouraged, as the preferred modern agent
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: production is banned.

options.text: It depletes ozone
Its production is banned
Only legacy systems remain

questions.explanation: Halon is an effective gaseous agent that depletes ozone. Its production is banned (EPA), so only legacy systems remain.
questions.discriminator_tested: Halon production is banned.

questions.stem: Which statement about argon as a fire suppression agent is NOT true?

options.text: It works by soaking the equipment in water
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: argon is a gas.

options.text: It is an inert gas
It works by reducing oxygen
It is safe for equipment

questions.explanation: Argon is an inert gas that displaces oxygen. It is safe for equipment and works by reducing oxygen.
questions.discriminator_tested: Argon is inert and works by oxygen reduction.

questions.stem: Which statement about NAF-S-III is NOT true?

options.text: It is a water-based sprinkler system
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: it is a chemical clean agent.

options.text: It is a chemical clean agent
It was developed as a replacement for halon
It is used as a gaseous suppressant

questions.explanation: NAF-S-III is a chemical clean agent developed as a replacement for halon.
questions.discriminator_tested: NAF-S-III replaces halon.

questions.stem: Which two statements about FM-200 are correct? (Choose two.)

options.text: It is a chemical clean agent (HFC-227ea)
It leaves no residue
It is water-based
It depletes ozone, as halon does
options.rationale: Ozone depletion is halon's problem; FM-200 was adopted partly to avoid it.

options.text: It is an inert gas, like argon
options.rationale: Argon is inert; FM-200 is a chemical agent.

questions.explanation: FM-200 is a chemical clean agent (HFC-227ea) with fast discharge. It is widely used in data centers and leaves no residue.
questions.discriminator_tested: FM-200: chemical clean agent, no residue.

questions.stem: Which statement about switch clustering is NOT true?

options.text: The failure of one switch always cuts connectivity for every user
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: removing that single point of failure is the point of clustering.

options.text: Several switches operate as one logical switch
It is a redundancy measure
It keeps traffic flowing through a single switch failure

questions.explanation: Switch clustering makes multiple switches operate as one logical switch, so a single switch failure doesn't cut connectivity.
questions.discriminator_tested: A single switch failure doesn't cut connectivity.

questions.stem: What is the goal of router redundancy with a first-hop redundancy protocol?

options.text: Keeping the default gateway available if one router fails
Only increasing bandwidth
Encrypting traffic
Replacing firewalls

questions.explanation: Router redundancy uses redundant routers and multiple paths with first-hop redundancy, so the default gateway stays available.
questions.discriminator_tested: The default gateway stays available.

questions.stem: Which two statements about firewall redundancy are correct? (Choose two.)

options.text: High-availability pairs can run active/standby or active/active
Sharing session state lets sessions survive a failover
A failover always drops every existing session
options.rationale: Not when the pair shares state.

options.text: A single firewall is enough for high availability
options.rationale: High availability needs at least two.

options.text: High availability requires a cold site

questions.explanation: Firewall redundancy uses high-availability pairs (active/standby or active/active) that share session state. State sharing lets sessions survive failover.
questions.discriminator_tested: State sharing lets sessions survive failover.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a form of server redundancy?

options.text: Running the server on a single power supply
options.rationale: Correct choice: that is a single point of failure.

options.text: Clustering
Load balancing
RAID

questions.explanation: Server redundancy uses clustering, load balancing, redundant power supplies, and RAID to remove single points of failure.
questions.discriminator_tested: Server redundancy removes single points of failure.

questions.stem: Which two statements about disaster recovery sites are correct? (Choose two.)

options.text: Faster recovery generally costs more
options.rationale: Correct: that is the core trade-off.

options.text: A hot site recovers faster than a cold site
A cold site has full equipment and live data
A warm site is the most expensive option
A cloud site needs no testing

questions.explanation: Disaster recovery sites are alternate locations for resuming operations. Choosing one is a trade-off between cost and recovery time, from a cold site (cheapest, slowest) to a hot site (fastest, most expensive).
questions.discriminator_tested: The trade-off is cost versus recovery time.

questions.stem: Which statement about a cold site is NOT true?

options.text: It can take over within minutes
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: it takes days to weeks.

options.text: It has power and connectivity
It has no equipment or data
It is the cheapest option

questions.explanation: A cold site is space with power and connectivity but no equipment or data. It is the cheapest and slowest option, taking days to weeks.
questions.discriminator_tested: Cold site: cheapest and slowest.

questions.stem: What separates a warm site from a hot site?

options.text: A warm site is partly equipped and restores data from backups; a hot site is fully equipped with near-real-time replication
A warm site is fully equipped; a hot site is empty space
They are the same
options.rationale: They differ in equipment, data, cost, and speed.

options.text: A warm site has no power

questions.explanation: A warm site is partly equipped, with data restored from backups, and sits in the middle in cost and time. A hot site is fully equipped with near-real-time replication.
questions.discriminator_tested: Warm restores from backups; hot replicates in near real time.

questions.stem: Which statement about a hot site is NOT true?

options.text: It is the cheapest type of DR site
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: it is the most expensive.

options.text: It is fully equipped
It has near-real-time replication
It is the fastest to take over

questions.explanation: A hot site is fully equipped with near-real-time data replication. It is the fastest and most expensive option.
questions.discriminator_tested: Hot site: fastest and most expensive.

questions.stem: Which two are characteristics of a cloud site for disaster recovery? (Choose two.)

options.text: Lower upfront cost, scaled on demand
Dependence on connectivity and on the provider
Servers must be bought in advance
options.rationale: Avoiding that is the point of using the cloud.

options.text: No testing is ever needed
options.rationale: It still has to be tested.

options.text: It is always the slowest option
options.rationale: It can be fast if it is well prepared.

questions.explanation: A cloud site is a recovery environment in a cloud provider, scaled on demand. It has lower upfront cost and is elastic, but it depends on connectivity, the provider, and testing.
questions.discriminator_tested: Cloud site: elastic, but depends on connectivity and the provider.

questions.stem: Choosing between active/active and active/passive, a company wants a standby server that sits idle and takes over only if the primary fails. It accepts idle resources in exchange for simple failover. Which design is this?

options.text: Active/passive
options.rationale: Correct: the standby waits idle until a failure.

options.text: Active/active
options.rationale: In active/active, both nodes serve traffic all the time.

options.text: A cold site
options.rationale: That is an empty alternate location.

options.text: Surge protection

questions.explanation: In active/active, all nodes serve traffic; in active/passive, a standby takes over on failure. Active/passive leaves resources idle; active/active loses capacity on failure.
questions.discriminator_tested: Active/passive leaves resources idle.

questions.stem: Which statement about multiple ISPs and diverse paths is NOT true?

options.text: Two ISP contracts guarantee diversity even if both cables run through one conduit
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: diversity must be physical.

options.text: It means using more than one provider
It needs physically separate routes
A shared conduit is a shared point of failure

questions.explanation: Multiple ISPs and diverse paths means more than one provider and physically separate routes. Diversity must be physical; two contracts in one conduit still share a failure point.
questions.discriminator_tested: Diversity must be physical.

questions.stem: Which statement about tabletop exercises is NOT true?

options.text: They involve actually failing over production systems
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: a tabletop is discussion only.

options.text: They are discussion only
The team talks through a scenario
They test roles and plans

questions.explanation: In tabletop exercises, the team talks through a disaster scenario without touching systems. They are discussion only and test roles and plans.
questions.discriminator_tested: Tabletop is discussion only.

questions.stem: Which statement about validation tests is NOT true?

options.text: They are discussion-only, with no systems touched
options.rationale: Correct choice because it is false: that is a tabletop exercise.

options.text: They are hands-on
They confirm that recovery procedures work
They actually exercise systems

questions.explanation: Validation tests are hands-on tests that confirm recovery procedures and systems work. Unlike a tabletop, they actually exercise systems.
questions.discriminator_tested: Validation actually exercises systems.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT typically part of a disaster recovery plan?

options.text: The marketing team's campaign calendar
options.rationale: Correct choice: unrelated to restoring IT.

options.text: Procedures for restoring systems
Data restoration steps
Recovery priorities and order

questions.explanation: A disaster recovery plan holds the documented procedures for restoring IT systems and data after a disruption. It is focused on IT restoration.
questions.discriminator_tested: The DRP is focused on IT restoration.

questions.stem: During a regional flood, staff work from a partner office, customer calls are rerouted, and payroll is run by hand while IT restores the servers. Which plan covers all of this?

options.text: The business continuity plan, which is broader than IT and includes the DRP
options.rationale: Correct: it keeps business operations going, not just IT.

options.text: Only the disaster recovery plan
options.rationale: The DRP covers only the IT restoration part.

options.text: A change request
A risk matrix

questions.explanation: A business continuity plan keeps critical business operations running during and after a disruption. It is broader than IT, and the DRP is part of it.
questions.discriminator_tested: The BCP is broader than IT; the DRP is part of it.
